podcast.body: A UK hit from their 1994 debut album "Definitely Maybe," written by Noel Gallagher. This song led to two separate lawsuits: one from The New Seekers (who had adapted a Coca-Cola commercial jingle into a hit) and another from members of Monty Python's Flying Circus, who claimed it sounded like a song from their 1973 TV sketch "How Sweet and Idiot." Oasis was ordered to make changes to the song, and guitarist Bonehead admitted the rip-off. "That's Shaker Maker, a UK hit for Oasis from 1994 and it was written by No Gallagher."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Featured on their debut album *Definitely Maybe*, this song from 1994 was found to be very similar to The New Seekers' 1970 hit "I'd Like to Teach the World to Sing," which originated from a Coca-Cola commercial. A lawsuit was filed, and Oasis did not strongly contest it. Liam Gallagher would sometimes "goof around by going into the lyrics of the Coke commercial" during live performances. Guitarist Bonehead admitted, "eh, we ripped it off." "It's Shaker Maker from the first Oasis album, definitely maybe, which was released in 1994."

podcast.body: Oasis songwriter Noel Gallagher "borrowed" the melody from The New Seekers' "I'd Like to Teach the World to Sing" for the verse of this Oasis hit. This instance demonstrates the lasting influence and cultural penetration of the jingle-turned-hit even decades later. "Decades later, he... let's say borrowed its melody for the verse of the Oasis hit Shaker Maker."
